value: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1), Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025
detail: Section 71119 of P.L. 119-21 created the Medicaid community engagement requirement (work requirement) as a condition of eligibility for specified Medicaid enrollees, adding section 1902(xx) to the Social Security Act.
notes: CRS Report R48755 identifies section 71119 as the Medicaid community engagement provision.

value: Non-pregnant adults ages 19-64 not entitled to or enrolled in Medicare
detail: Applies to individuals eligible for or enrolled in the Medicaid adult group (the ACA expansion group) or in certain section 1115 demonstrations providing minimum essential coverage. CMS reports 43 states plus DC cover these populations and must implement; U.S. territories are not subject.

value: 80 hours per month (about 20 hours per week)
detail: Applicable individuals must demonstrate 80 hours per month of qualifying activities, or satisfy the income alternative, or qualify for an exemption.

value: Work; community service; work program; at least half-time educational program; or any combination totaling 80 hours
detail: Individuals may combine activities to meet the 80-hour requirement.
notes: Federal definitions at 42 CFR 435.552(b): community service must be a structured public/nonprofit program that tracks hours; a work program excludes a stand-alone supervised job-search program (job search may only be a subsidiary activity under half the hours). Less-than-half-time school hours may be combined (credit hours x 3 x 4.33 weeks).

value: Monthly income of at least 80 x the federal hourly minimum wage ($580 per month in 2026)
detail: An individual can satisfy the requirement for a month with monthly income at or above 80 times the federal minimum wage instead of logging hours. Federal regulation 42 CFR 435.552(f)(2) measures that monthly income as the individual's MAGI-based income for their MAGI-based household (42 CFR 435.603) - so unearned MAGI income (net rental, interest, capital/trading gains) counts; California statute Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(e)(6) (AB 2161) uses the same MAGI-based method. DHCS member materials describe it as income from any source.
notes: Federal minimum wage $7.25 x 80 = $580. DHCS outreach letter: income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes). MAGI-based measurement re-verified 2026-10-18 against eCFR 42 CFR 435.552(f) and AB 2161 text; earlier DHCS 'total gross income' phrasing was preliminary (see FL-06).

value: Average monthly income of at least $580 over the preceding 6 months
detail: The 6-month averaging route in federal law/regulation is for a 'seasonal worker' as described in Internal Revenue Code 45R(d)(5)(B): average monthly MAGI-based income over the preceding 6 months of at least $580 (42 CFR 435.552(g)). DHCS preliminary/member wording also describes averaging for people whose hours change frequently or with fluctuating income - whether mere income fluctuation (e.g., variable trading gains) qualifies without seasonal-worker status is flagged (FL-11).
notes: DHCS H.R. 1 Implementation Plan and MEDIL I26-25 describe averaging more broadly; do not assume variable Kalshi gains can be averaged - confirm with the county.

value: Work = work for money, in-kind work, or unpaid work (other than community service); self-employment counts
detail: 42 CFR 435.552(b) defines work as work in exchange for money, work in exchange for goods or services (in-kind), and unpaid work other than community service. The CMS-2454-IFC preamble (91 FR 33348) states individuals need not be employees: people who work for themselves by starting/owning a business or as independent contractors meet the definition. DHCS ACWDL 25-30 likewise lists 'at least 80 hours of work' as including self-employment.
notes: Replaces the earlier out-of-state citation with the controlling federal definition + California ACWDL 25-30. Whether hours trading one's own account or managing one's own rentals are 'work' is still not addressed officially - see FL-02/FL-12. Trading gains are not self-employment earnings for tax purposes (IRS Topic 429), which is a separate question from the Medicaid work definition.

value: No later than January 1, 2027 (states may implement earlier)
detail: CMS states that states must generally implement the requirement no later than January 1, 2027; some states began earlier (for example Nebraska on May 1, 2026).
notes: CRS describes the effective date as December 31, 2026 or earlier at state option; see flagged items for the date-framing difference.

value: CMS-2454-IFC issued June 1, 2026; published in the Federal Register June 3, 2026 (91 FR 33348); effective July 31, 2026
detail: Interim final rule with comment period implementing section 1902(xx) of the Social Security Act; comment period closed July 31, 2026.

value: At application and at renewal; states may verify more frequently
detail: States verify compliance of applicable individuals at application, at renewal, and at state option at more frequent periodic intervals. California preliminary guidance (ACWDL 25-30) verifies only at application and six-month renewal, and states counties shall not assess the requirement merely because a member reports a change in circumstances.

value: California: applicants - the month immediately before application; enrollees - any one month between determinations
detail: Federal framing: new applicants meet the requirement for at least one month before applying; existing beneficiaries for one or more months between renewals. California law (Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(d), as amended by AB 2161) fixes the California test: an applicant must demonstrate engagement for the one month immediately preceding the application month; an enrolled person must demonstrate it for any one month between their most recent (re)determination and the next scheduled redetermination. It is therefore NOT an every-month test in California. ACWDL 25-30 gives worked examples (e.g., one qualifying month out of six at renewal suffices; months need not be consecutive).
source_name: California Legislative Information - AB 2161 (Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(d))
notes: Corrects any 'each month' phrasing elsewhere. If an applicant first becomes compliant while the application is pending, ACWDL 25-30 sets aid to begin the first day of the month after the compliance month, with earlier months denied (preliminary guidance).

value: 30-calendar-day cure period, then denial or disenrollment; reapplication allowed at any time
detail: If a state cannot verify compliance it must send a notice of noncompliance and provide 30 calendar days to demonstrate compliance or that the requirement does not apply; failing that, the application may be denied or the individual disenrolled. Disenrolled individuals may reapply at any time and are assessed on reapplication. California adds: coverage continues during the 30-day period (and at renewal, active eligibility is maintained at least through the end of that month); notice is deemed received 5 days after its date; self-attested non-receipt is good cause; denial/disenrollment occurs no later than the end of the following month, only after checking every other basis of eligibility and offering a fair hearing (AB 2161, Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(k)-(n)).
notes: No fixed lockout period appears in the CMS fact sheet. See also CA-14: California preliminary guidance allows return without a new application during a 90-day cure period after discontinuance once compliance is shown.

value: Expansion adults renew eligibility every 6 months instead of every 12
detail: Section 71107 of P.L. 119-21 requires states to conduct eligibility redeterminations for the MAGI New Adult Group every six months, effective January 1, 2027. Tribal members, pregnant or 12-month postpartum members, and children are not subject.
notes: California begins six-month checks March 1, 2027 (see California implementation table).

value: Compliance turns on hours of qualifying activity or monthly income, not on having a job or earned income
detail: $0 earned income does not by itself disqualify or satisfy the requirement; DHCS member materials allow income from any source to satisfy the $580 monthly standard.

value: $325.6 billion reduction in federal Medicaid outlays FY2025-FY2034
detail: CBO also estimated the community engagement provision would result in an average of 4.5 million more uninsured people per year FY2027-FY2034.

value: CMS released initial guidance to states in December 2025
detail: CMS issued a Center for Medicaid and CHIP Services Information Bulletin on implementing work and community engagement requirements on December 8, 2025.
source_name: CMS guidance via DHCS Tracking page

item: Losing Medi-Cal for noncompliance blocks Covered California financial help
value: No subsidized Covered California fallback if denied/disenrolled solely for work-rule noncompliance
detail: DHCS member outreach letter (MEDIL I26-25): 'If you lose Medi-Cal because you did not meet these rules, you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California. That means you would have to pay the full cost of new health insurance.' ACWDL 25-30 states the same for applicants and requires evaluation for all other Medi-Cal programs instead. This is distinct from having MAGI above Medi-Cal limits, where subsidized Covered California remains available with no work test.
source_name: DHCS MEDIL I26-25 member outreach letter (Sept 11, 2026)
notes: Practical consequence: do not treat subsidized marketplace coverage as a safety valve for failing the Medi-Cal work rule at MAGI at or below 138% FPL. Reapplying for Medi-Cal at any time remains allowed.

value: Agency may convert monthly MAGI-based income under $580 into work hours (income / $7.25) to combine toward 80 hours
detail: 42 CFR 435.552(e)(2): if monthly income is below 80 x federal minimum wage and the agency lacks documentation of hours worked, the agency may calculate work hours by dividing MAGI-based monthly income by the federal minimum wage, using a reasonable method to allocate hours between household members; those hours can be combined with other activities. Whether/how California will use this option has not been confirmed in published DHCS guidance reviewed.
notes: Federal option verified; California adoption unverified - ask the county before relying on a partial-income + partial-hours combination.
